description_en: Jothā Bāhāḥ is a branch of Rudravarṇa Mahāvihāra (also known as Uku Bāhāḥ). It is situated in an entirely enclosed courtyard in Thainā Ṭola at the western edge of the street which leads to Thainā from Saugala crossroad.The Bāhāḥ is raised 90 cm above this courtyard, and is furnished with steps that lead up to a three bayedphalcācontaining an image of a four-handed Māhākāla on its right wall. The Phalcā has been made narrower with brick infill walls. The main shrine building faces east and can be seen from the Phalcā. The main west wing of the shrine has three storeys. It can be entered through an intricately carved latticed door at the centre of the ground floor wall, which is flanked by two lattice windows (tikijhyāḥ). The lattice work of these windows has partly been replaced by themāneprayer wheel. Above the windows, one can find two wall paintings: the one on the left-hand side shows Meghanāda, a legendary prince from (Sri) Lanka, while the one on the right displays Rāvaṇa. Both are painted in the act of performing a scarifice (yajña). These paintings are dated to around 1944.The sanctum contains a statue of Akṣobhya Buddha facing east as well as statues of Amoghapāśa Lokeśvara, Ārya Tarā, Prajñāpāramitā and Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara.On the first floor of the Bāhāḥ, one can find a window with a row of three or five small openings (pāsukājhyaḥ), emphasized by an aedicule on either side. The entire courtyard building is furnished with lattice windows on the first floor, and encircled by an overhanging balcony. The lattice work and small central window of the balcony are interrupted at the southeast corner due to the new RCC building structure. The balcony has also been damaged at the northwest corner. The damaged north wing is now protected by two raking shores. The roof is made of tiles and above it there is a smallcaitya-shaped pinnacle. The courtyard can be accessed through a carved wooden door situated at the eastern wing. Above the main entrance is apāsukhājhyaḥand above this is a blind window (gāḥjhyāḥ).The larger courtyard of thebāhāmeasures 10 x 10 m and is 30 cm beneath the level of the Phalcā. Within this courtyard, one can find aśikharakūṭa caitya, a statue of the donor, adharmadhātu maṇḍalaand avedīarranged on an east-west axis in front of the main shrine building. In the northern wing of the Bāhāḥ one can find anotherpāsukhājhyāḥon the first floor, with a long wooden stick below it.Śākya(VS 2036, 40) mentions that the stick was used to support an umbrella which was unfurled in honour of Śrīnivāsa Malla when he was invited to thisbāhāḥ.Locke(1985, 110) informs us that thesaṅghaof this Bāhāḥ consists of four households of theŚākyasof Uku Bāhāḥ of the Mahā Bu lineage. The members of thesaṅghaact as caretakers (dyaḥpālā) in the shrine on a monthly rotational basis. The service passes through the four households. Thesaṅghahas one elder to observe the anniversary of the Bāhāḥ on the third day of the bright half of the month of Vaiśākha.According to the copper inscription attached to the façade, Jothā Bāhāḥ was established by Yodhā in 1653 CE (NS 773). It seems that Yodhā was also known as Jothāju, and so the monastery also became known as Jothā Bāhāḥ. Yodhā was the eldest son of Manikaju and the great grandson of Abhayarāja, who also established a shrine of Mahābuddha.Acharya(2004, 152-153) claims that Jothāju was a merchant who had a shop in Tibet. However, the members of the monastery believe that he was a sculptor who spent his earnings to establish this Bāhāḥ.
description_ne: गर्भगृहको दायाँ रावणले र बायाँ मेघनाथले यज्ञ गरेको चित्र लिखिएको छ । यी चित्रहरू विसं २००१ सालतिर मात्र लिखिएका हुन् । बौद्ध विहारमा हिन्दू चित्रको उपस्थितिलाई विशेष रूपमा हेर्न सकिन्छ ।विहार प्रांगणमा एउटा शिखरकूट चैत्य रहेको छ । चैत्यको पछाडि पूर्वतिर दाताको सालिक रहेको छ । सालिकको पूर्वतिर यज्ञशाला र धर्मधातु रहेको छ । विहारको उत्ततिर रहेको पासुखा झ्यालको तलतिर लामो काठको दण्डी राखिएको छ । यसलाई राजा श्रीनिवास मल्ललाई यस विहारमा निमन्त्रणा गर्दा ओढाइएको छत्रको दण्डी भनिन्छ ।यो विहार नेसं ७७३ मा जोथाजु (जोधाजु) शाक्यले स्थापना गरेका थिए । जोथाको अर्थ जेठो हो । मनिकजुको जेठो सन्तान हुनाले उनलाई जोथाजु भनिएको थियो । जोथाजु महाबुद्धको मन्दिर स्थापना गर्ने अभयराजका पनाति थिए । आचार्य (2004: 152-153) ले जोथाजुलाई तिब्बतमा कोठी रहेका व्यापारी भनेका छन् । तर यस विहारका सदस्यहरूका अनुसार जोथाजु मूर्ति बनाउने कालिगढ थिए । आफ्नो सीपबाट आर्जन गरेको सम्पत्तिबाट यो विहार बनाएका थिए ।

historical_events.event_description: Construction of the Jothā Bāhāḥ. On the right side of the main shrine, a copper plate inscription informs visitors of the establishment of the monastery. The inscription states that this Bāhāḥ, named Jayaśrī Vihāra, was established on Wednesday 3rd of the bright moon of Vaiśākha in NS 773. Moreover, it states that it was established by Yodhā, together with his wife Jayantī and their their daughter Śirī, as well as their sons Ratna, Amu, Ratnasiṃha, and Cintāmaṇi.

Vajrācārya(1999,151) states that on Thursday, 8th of the bright half of Śrāvaṇa, NS 787, Jothāju sent an invitation to King Śrīnivāsa Malla and performed asamyak mahādāna. The king was seated in a throne made of gold, which can now be found in the Patan Museum. Every year on the full moon day of Jyeṣṭha (Jyā Punhi) this throne is placed in the Kṛṣṇa temple of Mangalbazar for exhibition.
Consecration of the images of Amoghapāśa Lokeśvara and Ārya Tārā on the sides of the main deity inside the sanctum.
Thisdharmadhātu maṇḍalawas consecrated in memory of the donor's deceased father Ratnajoti and mother Jamunā Devi. The donor's name is abbreviated as Jo. Pu. Hma. A.
